name: Christmas Light Takedown
metaTitle: Christmas Light Takedown Service | Ontario & GTA Homes
metaDescription: Damage-free Christmas light takedown for London Ontario and GTA homes, scheduled January through early February around winter weather. Free quote today.
heroIntro: Careful, damage-free removal of your holiday lights once the season ends, with optional storage so you never touch a ladder in winter.
intro: Getting lights up is the fun part, getting them down safely in January is where most homeowners lose enthusiasm. Our takedown service removes your roofline, tree and shrub lighting the same way it was installed, carefully, with property-safe methods that leave clips and cords intact for reuse next year. Whether we installed your lights originally or another company did, our crew can take down an existing display, working from what is actually on your home rather than a set of our own notes.

Timing depends on the weather. Ontario winters mean roofs can be icy well into February, so we schedule takedowns from January through early February, whenever conditions make it safe to get on a roof or use our aerial lifts. We are not in a rush to rip lights down the day after New Year's if the forecast says otherwise, we would rather wait a week and do it safely than risk a fall or damage to your home.
included: Scheduled removal window between January and early February
Damage-free removal from roofline, trees and shrubs
Careful handling of clips, cords and timers for reuse
Property protection around landscaping and walkways during removal
Bucket truck or aerial lift access for tall rooflines and mature trees
Available whether or not we installed your original display

sections.heading: How takedown scheduling works
sections.text: Once the holidays are over, we start booking takedown windows for our full-season and installation customers first, then open remaining slots to anyone who needs a standalone removal. We watch the weather closely, since a roof coated in ice or snow is not a safe place for a ladder or a lift, so exact dates shift year to year between January and early February. If you need your lights down by a specific date for an event or a home sale, mention it when you book and we will do our best to prioritize your property.

sections.heading: What determines the cost
sections.text: Takedown pricing depends on how much lighting is up, roofline length, whether trees or shrubs are included, and the height and accessibility of your home, the same factors that shape an installation quote. A standalone takedown for a display we did not install may take a little longer since our crew has to figure out the layout on site rather than working from our own design notes. We confirm the cost before the visit so there are no surprises when the crew arrives.

sections.heading: What to expect on takedown day
sections.text: Our crew removes lighting the same careful way it went up, unclipping strands from the roofline, trees and shrubs without tugging on shingles, fascia or bark. Cords, timers and light strands are coiled and boxed so they survive storage in good condition rather than getting knotted into a garbage bag in the corner of your garage. If you added optional storage, everything goes straight into our inventory system so it is inspected and ready to reinstall the following season without you lifting a bin or sorting through tangled strands yourself.

pricing: Takedown is priced based on how much lighting needs to come down and how accessible your home is, similar to the factors that set an installation price. Customers who booked Full Season Holiday Service have takedown bundled into their original quote at no extra step. Standalone takedown requests, including displays we did not originally install, get a custom quote once we know the scope.

faq.q: When do you take down Christmas lights?
faq.a: Takedowns run from January through early February, depending on weather and whether it is safe to access the roof. We would rather wait a week for ice to clear than risk a fall, so exact dates vary by property and by how the winter is shaping up rather than following a fixed calendar date every year.

faq.q: Can you take down lights that another company installed?
faq.a: Yes. Our crew can remove an existing display even if we were not the ones who installed it originally. Pricing may reflect the extra time needed to work out the layout on site, since we do not have our own design notes to reference, but the removal itself is handled with the same care.

faq.q: Will takedown damage my roof, siding or trees?
faq.a: No. We remove lighting the same careful way it goes up, unclipping strands rather than pulling or yanking on them, and using bucket trucks or aerial lifts for tall rooflines and mature trees so nothing gets forced loose or leaves marks on shingles, fascia or bark. The same property-safe approach we use during installation carries through to removal, since the crew and equipment are the same.

faq.q: Do you store the lights after takedown, or hand them back to me?
faq.a: Storage is optional and separate from takedown itself. If you would like your strands cataloged, inspected and kept until next season instead of going back into your garage, ask about year-round storage when you book your removal. Otherwise, we hand everything back to you cleanly coiled and packed once the crew finishes taking your display down.
